references.observed: The 2022 photograph shows green rafter ends and round ceramic tile ends on all four eaves. The photo account places the stele west of the Silkworm Deity Temple. The west-side draft tests relative position and terrain. It does not establish the shelter footprint.

references.note: The courtyard photo shows several paving joints turning across the apron and irregular slab widths. Round tile ends follow regular courses in the upturned roof. The separate joints are visible over a nearly plain, dark fired-clay surface.

visualBrief: A 1.94 m round-headed grey stone with three incised south-face title characters, a wave-relief base with two 0.30 m deep planter pockets, and a four-post green shelter beneath a grey tiled roof. Close-up geometry shows the faded seal outline, the fine fracture beside the title and the long weathered recess on the north face. A freestanding bronze-toned interpretation sign stands to the right of the shelter. The bronze plaque on the south railing has a stepped rim, concealed mounts and a hand-traced heading and the photographed two-column poem layout at close range. Green painted rafters support the shelter’s curved eaves. The round grey ceramic tile ends are modeled at close range. A low stone curb supports the shelter inside a flagstone apron. The apron extends east toward the walk and leaves soil around the sign. The roof uses the shared fired-clay surface, with geometry defining the ribs and round tile ends. The apron includes staggered flagstone joints. The freestanding bronze-toned sign follows the photographed rounded lower profile, raised perimeter, paired round posts and turned caps.
nativeAxes: +X is east and +Z is south at heading 0. The title and visitor sign face +Z.

placementEvidence.scope: The modeled shelter sits on the approximate apron inferred from historical aerial images and the retained path edge. The conservation account and current photos support this site. The inscription faces south. Canopy obscures the exact roof outline and footings. Fine inscriptions, rafter dimensions and apron width are estimates.

visitorRoute.note: The photo sequence moves from the waterfront hall and the Silkworm Deity Temple to the stele, then to the Tuancheng Lake sign. Separate frames confirm the order. They leave the connecting path and distances uncertain.

mapFitTrial.conclusion: The modeled paving and sign clear the mapped building and water polygons at the trial coordinate. The extract leaves the shelter and its immediate visitor path unmapped.

parkOverview.note: The park overview identifies the Farming and Weaving garden between the canal and Kunming Lake. It has no shelter-level marker.

priorTrial.reason: This point is east of the temple, in conflict with the visitor account.

currentTrial.datumBasis: An initial pass at 55.33 m left the rendered landcover above the paving. The trial uses the measured overlay height and leaves a small margin for the slab. This elevation is specific to the trial terrain.

westOfTemple.conclusion: The new trial is consistent with the documented side of the temple. Several positions along the corridor also clear PMTiles. Canopy still hides the shelter and path junctions.

eastApron.measurement: The four shelter posts define the photo frame. Their 3.60 by 2.52 m model spacing and 3.07 m clear height set the approximate scale. The walk edge was projected onto level ground 0.19 m below the curb. The second image has a shorter and more oblique visible path segment.
eastApron.note: The model extends the flagstones toward the walk without drawing its route beyond the shelter. Both images support the orientation of the path relative to the shelter. PMTiles lacks the corresponding local path, and the geographic anchor remains provisional.

overhead.fit: The exposed section is in the western garden. The nearest visible path segment runs roughly north to south and is west of the former draft pin. The photographs show the approach beside the east apron. The segment could be a continuation or neighboring path under the canopy.

westWalkTrial.positionBasis: Keep the photographed paving to the east of the shelter. The uncovered path guides the trial. Neither the exact path segment nor the shelter footprint is identifiable through the canopy.

southFacingCheck.basis: Subtract the ground-photo walk angle from the bearing of the possible walk in the overhead view. Both estimates agree with the museum’s south-facing description. The match assumes this is the photographed walk. The two estimates do not constrain position along it.

apronContinuity.basis: The archival rectangle sits west of the garden walk and north of its bend toward the temple. A pale edge remains visible there in the 2018 image. Ground photographs before and after sheltering show the same masonry wall near the title stone. The conservation account says the park built a shelter for this stone. Taken together, these support approximate continuity at the archival apron. The present roof outline and individual footings are obscured in overhead imagery.

continuitySources.observation: The account says the Summer Palace erected protective shelters for exposed monuments including the Farming and Weaving Stele starting in 2017.
The 2022 photo shows the covered stele beside the narrow east walk with a fieldstone wall behind the pavilion. The traveler approaches from the temple side.
The open and covered photographs show the round-headed slab, wave plinth and capped fieldstone wall. The open photograph capture date is unknown.

postArchiveImages.observation: The north–south walk remains visible with a pale apron immediately on its west. Low resolution and branches obscure the central object.

An exposed pale edge projects west from the same garden-walk bend, north of the branch toward the temple. Its position agrees with the open apron in the 2005–2010 images. Canopy covers the western end.
The winter image locates the canal lock, temple and the path. The evergreen canopy at the apron leaves the roof less distinct than the garden controls.

interpretationSign.observation: The freestanding sign beside the east walk has two round posts, a raised border and two shallow shoulders on either side of a curved central drop.
interpretationSign.limitation: The proportions are estimated from the photographs. The inscription is too small to transcribe from these views.

railingPlaquePoems.observation: The bronze railing plaque separates a seven-character heading from two introductory lines and its left and right poem columns. The close-up mesh uses a simplified trace of the ink below the rule. The contact footer is outside the crop.

walkSequence.observation: The photographer reports turning back from the stele to reach Fortress Lake. The park sign shows a map pin at the lake path junction. The sequence relates the stele to the temple and path junction without showing the connecting walk in a single frame.
